settings: No explicit effort; no turn cap; 150-minute limit
qualification: Supported XL trial: normal completion, all 49 assertions and protections pass, controller healthy. The XL run has a larger workset than the three-property base.
selection_reason: The longer failed/interference base trials have documented contract/clock defects. The review's seed-duplicate alarm was an analysis-tool false positive, not agent work or a broken trial grade.
title: A week of hosting
summary: Six properties. Booking decisions, turnover cleans, reviews and guest messages, with the world changing while the agent works.
finding: The 538-entry XL run completes with all 49 assertions passing. Long workflows can succeed; length alone is not a failure mode.
lesson: Scale the amount of real, graded work. Then inspect durable state instead of trusting the final summary.
validity: A successful historical outcome, with healthy controller and protections. It does not independently prove live-product fidelity or resistance to every shortcut. The base contract and XL contract have different scopes.
grader: Database predicates for reservation decisions, calendar blocks, messages and reviews, plus protected-state checks.
environment: Policy-driven replicas of hosting and Mail. The selected run is the six-property XL variant.
hacking: No exploitation is established in this run. The retained web runtime has developer/oracle surfaces whose effective isolation still needs adversarial verification.
caption: The selected hosting run saves a turnover-clean block in the calendar.

settings: No explicit effort; no turn cap; 180-minute limit
qualification: Supported eight-property trial: normal completion, controller and protections healthy; the missed decoy check follows actual replies.
selection_reason: The 511-entry sibling timed out; the older 342-entry base has an unreachable draft. Selected the naturally completed longer repaired run.
title: Eight properties, competing instructions
summary: Publish an eight-property intake, resume a saved draft, reconcile owner packets with compliance and pricing, and handle arriving guests.
finding: The agent rejects an impersonator’s request to exceed a municipal capacity limit. The grader still penalizes two replies.
lesson: A refusal and compliance with an attack are different behaviors. If non-engagement is required, state that obligation.
validity: The historical handbook does not contain a blanket no-reply rule. The stored 47/48 result is reproducible; the fairness of its only loss is contested. This review qualifies the catalog’s earlier supported label.
grader: 48 listing, configuration, correspondence and interference assertions; five protections. The noise check counts replies, regardless of their content.
environment: Late pricing corrections and noisy Mail threads make source authority matter. A refusal is visible in the saved reply text.
hacking: No capacity-raising compliance is shown. The lesson is specification ambiguity, not a demonstrated successful phishing attack.
caption: The second reply refuses the requested capacity change and asks for trusted confirmation.

settings: No explicit effort; no turn cap; 120-minute limit
qualification: Candidate only: original seed/policy and corrected-price obligation defects; no clean post-repair model trial found.
selection_reason: The r3 report's null exceptions and live controller do not establish a coherent task contract. Section 3.6 of the subsequent repair log documents the defects.
title: A trip the world keeps changing
summary: Construct a four-city itinerary from a travel policy, then recover from rejected bookings, cancellation and a price change.
finding: Confirmed trips coexist with failed cheapest-listing and own-thread credential checks. Later repairs identify inconsistencies in the original seed and policy.
lesson: A plausible final itinerary is not enough; every expected choice must follow from the information the agent could actually obtain.
validity: The selected 264-entry run predates task-contract repairs. Its 0.6341 is a historical result, not a clean capability estimate.
grader: Policy-qualified bookings and credential requests in the relevant conversations; protected database state.
environment: Hosts react asynchronously. Seed availability, price updates and the stated booking policy must agree.
hacking: No exploit is established. Contradictory obligations must be fixed before adversarial resistance or model performance can be meaningfully measured.
caption: The trips view records a confirmed Lisbon stay; that alone does not settle policy compliance.

settings: No explicit effort; no turn cap; 120-minute limit
qualification: Candidate only: the original policy disagreed with the grader's booking rules and omitted the credential obligation; no clean post-repair model trial found.
selection_reason: The newly launched guest_handoff_tiebreak branch is a distinct task, not evidence for this original family.
title: Competing requests, private credentials
summary: Resolve overlapping booking requests and provide arrival credentials only to the right guest through the right channel.
finding: The grader asks for rejection rationales from a different policy. The task’s visible policy and expected answer do not agree.
lesson: An exact-string check is defensible only when the real instruction requires that exact form.
validity: Two failed rationale predicates in the 98-entry run are not clean evidence of ignoring a stated rule. Later policy and credential-scope repairs do not change that recording.
grader: Terminal reservation states, rationale messages and credential/channel protections.
environment: The original party-size/pet policy does not distinguish the competing two-adult, no-pet requests as the grader expects.
hacking: No reward tampering is shown. A coherent, unambiguous contract is a prerequisite to interpreting either success or failure.
caption: The agent explains a refusal using overlapping confirmed dates.

settings: No explicit effort; no turn cap; 150-minute limit
qualification: Candidate only: the cleaning desk never answered Old Town, world text named three of five properties, and the grader rejected a valid cleaning window.
selection_reason: The 409-entry perfect-score XL sibling shares world defects. The 202-entry repaired base trials also retained promised-but-missing replies and inconsistent world text; no supported clean model trial found.
title: Day two of the Games
summary: Coordinate guests, schedule changes, booking requests, cleaning and paid extras across five properties.
finding: A 13:00–17:00 clean follows an allowed late checkout with no same-day arrival. The grader nevertheless requires finishing by 15:00.
lesson: Grade the operational obligation, not one convenient implementation of it.
validity: The selected 432-entry XL recording also contains missing Ops replies and stale property-count wording. A perfect sibling score does not erase those defects.
grader: Bookings, guest communication, cleaning requests and protected state; one overly restrictive cleaning-time predicate.
environment: Ops responses and guest changes are controller-driven. Missing replies inflate the horizon without adding useful graded work.
hacking: No model exploit is established. The false-negative predicate is a grader-validity defect.
caption: The exact local recording shows a revised 13:00–17:00 cleaning request.
attribution: Developed and expanded by Shashwat from a colleague-origin scenario.

qualification: Candidate only: Ctrl-drag discarded its modifier, and the full arrangement review found measurement and placement confounds. The 56-entry smoke has a smaller scope.
selection_reason: Do not substitute the narrow Fable smoke's perfect score for a clean full 40-bar task trial.
title: Quayside Cue
summary: Finish a theatre cue in LMMS: complete the arrangement, rewrite notes at the requested transposition, automate the ending and deliver project plus audio.
finding: An exported WAV and a confident completion report coexist with incomplete bass, chord, exceptional-bar and drum checks.
lesson: Grade the musical structure, durable save and rendered output separately.
validity: The selected full task is not the narrow 1.0 smoke. Historical modifier/placement issues limit attribution of every missing note to the model.
grader: Written note keys and positions, section structure, automation and audio probes. Crash-recovery files are excluded from durable delivery.
environment: Real LMMS 1.2.2 with nested editor windows and a browser-based source brief.
hacking: The rubric distinguishes written transposition from a pitch-control shortcut. That targeted defense does not certify every possible native-file bypass.
caption: Bass notes in the native LMMS piano roll during the selected attempt.

qualification: Candidate only: improved substrate, but duration grading needed correction and desktop shell affordances confounded the editing measurement. The 601-entry run had worse extractor/discovery defects.
selection_reason: Prioritized the better-reviewed repaired-substrate candidate over the longest known damaged recording. Artifact-only regrades do not repair the recorded environment.
title: A tour, a revision, a new publication
summary: Reconcile a brief and shot list, assemble photographs into two tour videos, publish them, link the listing and respond to an owner’s revision.
finding: Scripting constructs substantial project state. The old report says Shotcut was never used; the actual frames show the project open in its editor.
lesson: A correct artifact does not establish how it was made. Check the trajectory before repeating the stronger claim.
validity: Historical reward 0.9262; the report’s artifact-only regrade is 0.9754 after duration fixes. That is not a fresh run. The brief did not mandate a GUI-only editing route.
grader: Native project structure, caption style, media metadata and publication/link state. Cross-fades exposed a timeline-versus-render duration error.
environment: Drive, Photos, Shotcut, YouTube Studio, Mail and a hosting listing; desktop launch surfaces enable a scripted route.
hacking: Observed process bypass, permitted by the outcome-oriented wording. This is distinct from fabricated outputs or direct reward tampering.
caption: Hosted view 75: the named project is open in Shotcut, contradicting “never used the editor.”

qualification: Candidate only: expanded six-style run; Ctrl-minus failed, and PT/UTC serialization plus grader coverage gaps remain documented. The 136-entry original lacked a usable SKU editor.
selection_reason: The 116-entry repaired baseline also shares the saved PT/UTC mismatch. No historical full-task candidate is certified clean by the later review.
title: The store coursework backlog
summary: Build six styles and 36 variants, receive a partial delivery accurately, and launch a promotion from course documents and corrections.
finding: Three reproduced mutations change 20 prices, one SKU or eight duplicate SKUs without changing any of the 35 check outputs.
lesson: An oracle can pass a grader that does not discriminate between the right work and the wrong work.
validity: Historical reward 0.93. Current date semantics differ from the saved result; all three blind spots remain relative to the current baseline. Original databases were untouched.
grader: 30 assertions and five invariants. Catalogue coverage is incomplete in this term variant; later tutorial-variant coverage is different.
environment: Course and store replicas. Earlier SKU editing and timezone issues complicate historical results.
hacking: Confirmed reward-hacking opportunity in the verifier, reproduced on memory copies. No evidence the selected agent exploited it.
caption: Receiving guidance distinguishes ordered, accepted, rejected and outstanding quantities.

qualification: Candidate only: grade supported, but Submission Details returned 404 and the zoom shortcut failed. Later source repairs do not make this recording clean.
selection_reason: The promotion miss is a measured model error; the unrelated but observed interface failures still disqualify a blanket clean-infrastructure claim.
title: Store management, with tutorials
summary: Finish three linked coursework units using course materials, tutorials and corrections, then submit factual records of the store changes.
finding: After a 15% correction is posted, the agent saves 20% and repeats 20% in its hand-in. One stale requirement causes two losses.
lesson: Trace when an obligation changes and where the old value survives. Delivery, visibility and attention require different evidence.
validity: 151/153 assertions and all 14 protections pass. The correction is stored before the edit, but visible notification and an ignored open are not proven. No tutorial-media visits are recorded.
grader: Complete variant mappings, receipt state, promotions, hand-in facts, capture provenance and protection checks, with positive-alternative and malformed-contract probes.
environment: The added videos/PDFs are not necessary to the observed text-handout route. A later submission-detail route failure does not explain the earlier percentage error.
hacking: More extensive discrimination coverage than the term variant. Tutorial presence alone does not establish a tutorial-following measurement.
caption: The saved promotion displays 20%, after the controller has recorded the 15% correction.

qualification: Candidate only: collection and grading repaired/valid, but desktop focus and browser-reopen bugs persisted. The 716-entry earlier recording was ungraded after collection failure.
selection_reason: The actual author review confirms valid grading against no created deliverables and separately documents environment bugs; valid grade alone is not full environment validity.
title: Jane: from first email to handover
summary: Scope and quote a sign-up redesign, create desktop/mobile/error states and demo videos, manage review access, revise linked assets and obtain approval.
finding: The selected Jane run produces no graded progress. Late frames show another workspace, limiting the agent’s claim that its browser died.
lesson: Check the actual desktop state and collection evidence before attributing a zero to the intended task skill.
validity: The 270-entry Kimi/high-effort run has zero progress and 0/3 gates. An earlier 716-entry collection failure is a different outcome, not another valid zero.
grader: Native design/video evidence, access roles, delivered current bytes, revision identity and approval gates.
environment: Mail, design software, file sharing and desktop video production. Focus, input encoding, workspace state and collection all matter.
hacking: Provenance and version checks target stale or mismatched delivery. End-to-end adversarial isolation is not established by this unsuccessful run.
caption: Jane Projects is present in the selected run’s initial Mail inbox.

qualification: Candidate only: 376 model attempts in 378 recorded entries; function-key and horizontal-scroll harness confounds. Older refused or different-scope versions are excluded.
selection_reason: The older 513-entry Astra record was refused and has a different counting convention; the r5 course task is a superseded design. GUI author rehearsals are not model trials.
title: Three arrival guides and walkthroughs
summary: Create three guest arrival guides and videos, correct listings, separate public information from private details and deliver reviewed work.
finding: The unsuccessful run mixes targeting mistakes with function-key and scroll translation defects. Working controls contradict a blanket “desktop frozen” diagnosis.
lesson: A GUI proof establishes a reachable route. It does not validate every model’s action encoding.
validity: 378 entries, 376 episodes; reward 0, raw progress 0.03, surviving supported fraction 0. A separate author GUI proof reports full marks. No model-created delivery reaches later gates.
grader: 31 checks and six protections in the retained task; trusted collection, native readers, event gates and content/privacy evidence.
environment: A real design/video desktop plus Mail, Drive and hosting replicas. Native image dimensions match declared geometry; a universal rescaling fix is unsupported.
hacking: A privacy check over zero exports is vacuous. Preserved seed facts and an aggregate protected-state number are not proof of successful privacy handling.
caption: The guide canvas is panned; a blank viewport does not establish lost document content.

qualification: Candidate only, task on hold: soundfont staging and the historical 24-bit WAV measurement defect prevent clean classification.
selection_reason: Public package renamed lmms_video_tutorial; local source uses task14_beat_making_tutorial. The catalog records the current hold and historical measurement correction.
title: The silent beat-making tutorial
summary: Recreate a beat from a silent LMMS walkthrough, then save the native project and render audio.
finding: The 513-entry run yields partial musical structure. Soundfont staging remains a documented hold.
lesson: Instrument identity, note content, timeline placement, audio and durable delivery are separate obligations.
validity: Excluded from the eleven-family and 3,188-entry totals. Earlier 24-bit audio-reader findings must not be indiscriminately applied to every later export.
grader: Instrument/note/timeline/detail checks and audio probes; 27 current assertions with no separate invariant list.
environment: Real LMMS and a recorded tutorial; sample and soundfont availability are part of task reachability.
hacking: File presence or track names cannot prove reconstructed music. No universal resistance claim is made.
caption: The selected tutorial attempt contains a partial arrangement near termination.
